context.guidance: Store Authentication Secrets with a current, salted, deliberately slow password hashing function, never with a plain or fast unsalted digest. Re-hash each existing record with the new function the next time the Data Principal authenticates. Rule 6(1)(a) requires protection of the Personal Data these secrets guard, and a weak hash removes that protection once the store is read.

value.fix: Stop putting the password digest (and the email) into the SQL string. Use a parameterized query that looks the user up by email only: models.sequelize.query('SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = ? AND deletedAt IS NULL', { replacements: [req.body.email || ''], model: UserModel, plain: true }), or use UserModel.findOne({ where: { email } }). Then check the password in application code with a slow, salted hash such as argon2id (for example argon2.verify(user.password, req.body.password)) or bcrypt with cost 12 or higher, instead of comparing against the fast unsalted digest from security.hash (MD5). Add a field that records which hash algorithm each row uses. On each successful login, if the row still holds the legacy digest, check it with a constant-time comparison, then immediately re-hash the plaintext with argon2id or bcrypt and save it, so old records are upgraded the next time each user logs in. Use the same argon2id or bcrypt hashing at signup and password change. Once the migration window ends, force a password reset for any records that were never upgraded.
